title.narrative: Improving public financial management for the green transition

description.narrative: Serbia is an upper middle-income country with a per capita income of US$ 9,215 in 2021. The country's economy and household incomes expanded following a significant fiscal adjustment in 2014-15, and the fiscal environment improved significantly up until 2019. In 2020, the economy contracted by 1 percent due to COVID-19, followed by a strong rebound in 2021 with growth accelerating to 7.4 percent. The proposed operation is aligned with and supports the focus areas and objectives of the Country Partnership Framework (CPF) 2022–2026.11 It provides support across High-Level Outcomes (HLOs) 1 and 2, specifically objectives 1.1 (structural reforms for greener growth), 1.2 (green investments and just transition), and 2.1 (strengthened public finance management at central and local levels). Improved performance on key PFM indicators has a direct impact on the optimal use of budget funds. In addition, enhanced fiscal transparency will increase trust in institutions. The operation's objective of improving the quality of key areas of PFM at financial and other agencies to support green growth will directly contribute to the wider objectives of the CPF. The PforR instrument including an IPF component has been identified as best suited to incentivize change combined with providing hand-holding support for achieving the agreed results and it logically complements the Green Transition DPO series (P177410). The DPO series targets legal and regulatory changes to set the green transition in motion, while the PforR provides incentives and hand-holding support for implementation of these legal reforms; and it enables a shared monitoring of results over a four-year time horizon. The IPF/TA component builds on the lesson from the previous PforR on Public Sector Modernization (P155172) that ensuring adequate handholding directly related to achieving DLRs is essential. Responding to the challenges outlined, the project includes two proposed Results Areas:Results Area 1: Strengthen fiscal resilience, transparency, and spending effectivenessThis will include 3 DLIs (3, 6, 7) focused on further strengthening fiscal resilience, using public expenditure management to enhance efficiency and a results focus, improve fiscal transparency, and improving the preparation and vetting of public investment projects. Results Area 2: Green the expenditure cycle and monitor GHG emissions for Serbia's green transitionThis will include 5 DLIs (1, 2, 4, 5, 8) focused on introducing and utilizing green criteria in PFM, PIM, and public procurement, and on strengthening systems for monitoring and reporting on GHG emissionsComplementing the changes incentivized by the DLIs/DLRs, the small IPF/TA component (EUR3.15m from the WB plus EUR3.15m from AFD) will provide handholding support, in line with lessons learned from the previous PforR. Direct handholding support is important to enable the achievement of results and to address bottlenecks where and when needed. Project management support is important as implementing the PforR and fulfilling monitoring, reporting, and verification requirements is time intensive and can be difficult to accomplish for existing counterpart staff without additional support that can be contracted. The IPF component will consist of TA -- including change management, training and peer learning, support for stakeholder engagement, and for managing the Program. The TA needs identified for the IPF component take into account what TA is currently programmed to be provided by other development partners; and it builds on ongoing TA provided by WB teams based on TFs in several areas (notably fiscal risk and public investment management). Each implementing institution will prepare their ToRs. DICEI will monitor TA needs and coordination with other development partner support for RA 1 and PFM related aspects of RA 2. The CFU will provide procurement support, following standard IPF rules. The Bank will review and provide non-objections to final ToRs and to the final selection of service providers. Where possible and sensible, TA delivery to civil servants will involve the National Academy of Public Administration (as the main provider or as a co-recipient of training materials etc.) to enable a wider reach/coverage of relevant public sector staff.
The Program Development Objective is to improve core PFM functions and institutional capabilities needed for Serbia's fiscal resilience and green transition.

baseline.value: No Green Budget Tagging in place based on a consistent methodology. Some preliminary identification of green expenditures was done for the 2022 budget.

target.value: Green budget tagging is established in Serbia and has been used for two consecutive budget cycles (2025 and 2026)

actual.value: Green Budget Tagging (GBT) Methodology and accompanying Implementation Roadmap were adopted by the Inter-ministerial Working Group (IMWG) and the MoF, and published on the website of the MoF on December 29 2023. Budget Instruction for preparation of the 2025 budget, issued by the MoF in July 2024, mandated application of the Methodology.

title.narrative: The share of green and climate responsive public investments in total capital expenditures is increased

baseline.value: The share of green public investments is not systematically monitored or reported on, and cannot be adequately assessed in the absence of a methodology and criteria (e.g. for considering capital projects partially or completely as green (including climate mitigation) or as enhancing climate resilience.

target.value: Green and climate-responsive capital expenditures reach 25% of all capital expenditures subject to the Decree on Capital Projects, as determined by (i) a review of the entire public investment portfolio for 2027, and (ii) an assessment of the share based on the criteria developed and approved

actual.value: Criteria for prescreening, appraisal, review of appraisal and selection of projects according to environmental/climate relevance will be adopted through five by-laws as required by the amended Decree on capital projects. All five by-laws were adopted.

title.narrative: Green and climate aspects are integrated into Public Policy Documents and the links between PPDs and budgets are strengthened

baseline.value: Green and climate aspects/considerations are limited to policy plans of the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

target.value: Over at least the last 12 months, all newly approved PPDs and PPD updates relevant for the Green Agenda are developed in accordance to the Guidelines and with the application of Calculator/Tool for costs calculations.

actual.value: The PPS has developed the guidelines on inclusion of green aspects into public policy documents (PPDs). The adoption and publication of the Guidelines was completed in July 2024, and the related DLR was verified.

title.narrative: Improved fiscal transparency and program-based budgeting, including gender disaggregation

baseline.value: Information on fiscal outturns and on performance indicators is published with long delays and does not effectively inform the annual budget preparationDisaggregation by gender (of allocation and results) remains little used.

target.value: Fiscal outturn information and program budget KPIs for at least three large budget users (including a focus on public sector efficiency and including disaggregation by gender) are published at least once within 12 months of budget adoption and analysis of costs and results achieved informs future annual budgets.

actual.value: The analysis of program budgets on expenditure efficiency, environmental, and gender specific aspects of performance, is in progress, and the corresponding DLR (DLR 6.1) was achieved in August 2024 and is being verified. The related DLR required three ministries to fulfil the requirement, and the support to ministries and assessment by the consultants hired from the IPF part of the project, related to the program budget for 2024 for the following ministries: Ministry of Mining and Energy, Ministry of Environmental Protection and Ministry of Labor, Employment, Veterans and Social Affairs.

title.narrative: Broadened use of green public procurement

baseline.value: 7 procurements across the national Government of Serbia applied green public procurement guidelines in 2021 (<3% of all tenders).

target.value: Across the 7 selected institutions, at least 15% of tenders in procurement process and contract implementation use green criteria as defined in the applicable guidelines (and report on % of volume)

actual.value: The percentage of green public procurement procedures implemented in 2023 accordance with the Green Public Procurement Guidelines, is 6.82% across selected institutions: MoEP, SEPA, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Ministry of Economy, and Administration for Joint Affairs. Ð¢here were 264 public procurements carried out in 2023 by 7 selected institutions, of which 18 were green public procurements, which is a percentage of 6.82% of the total number of procurements for 2023.

title.narrative: An MRV system for GHG emissions is operational and in use

baseline.value: MRV system designed but not yet operational; final regulatory steps will be completed by March 2023 as required by the 2021 Law on Climate Change.

target.value: An MRV system for GHG is operational and in use.

actual.value: The MoEP has adopted six bylaws on the Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) of national emissions and installation-level emissions.

title.narrative: Implementing effective fiscal risk monitoring and reporting

baseline.value: Methodologies for monitoring fiscal risks have been adopted, but not yet fully used.

target.value: The Government publishes the 2027-2029 Fiscal Strategy and the adopted annual budget for 2027 (i) setting out quantified forward looking fiscal risks; and (ii) with the narrative part of the annual budget specifying fiscal adjustments to be made in case that said fiscal risks materialize (such as the use of contingency funds, budget re-allocations).

actual.value: Quarterly fiscal risk reports will be prepared starting with Q4 2024. This target date of Q4 2024 for producing fiscal risk reports was also included in the PFM Reform Program 2021-2025, as revised in December 2023. The Bank provided templates for the fiscal risk reports under the stand-alone project which supports the fiscal risk monitoring. It should be noted that starting from November 1, 2024 the fiscal risk monitoring function will shift from the Fiscal Risk Monitoring Department to the Budget Department. The Budget Department has substantial experience and expertise, and the Bank team is working with them to support the transition where needed.

title.narrative: Improving management of public investments and assets

baseline.value: Proposed public investment projects are not systematically reviewed in terms of readiness and (financial) realism.

target.value: The Ministry of Finance issues an opinion on financial and implementation aspects on all projects submitted for selection and recommends a List of Priority Projects based on criteria prescribed by the GoS and final section is largely based on the recommendations given.

actual.value: PIMIS is operational. The MoF expects the proportion of project implementation plans and progress reports being implemented through the PIMIS to be above the 30 percent benchmark during 2024, as defined in the Program results framework. According to the MoF program progress report for January-June 2024, 56 percent of capital projects fulfilled the requirement as of June 2024.
